about.title: Guadalupe Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Guadalupe is a small city, but its collision numbers aren't zero — public records show 8 injury crashes and 14 injured people in the most recent year, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing up more often than other times. Guadalupe Street, 11th Street, W Main Street, and Route 166 see the heaviest reported traffic and, with it, the most collisions. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the period right after matters. Insurance adjusters often reach out quickly, sometimes asking for a recorded statement before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result — we simply connect injured people in Guadalupe with an independent attorney who can review the details, explain your options under California law, and work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover something.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or public bus — is involved. Waiting can quietly cost you options.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, which means the other side's insurer may try to pin partial blame on you to reduce what they owe. An attorney can help make sure your side of the story is documented before that narrative gets set.

items.title: What You Say Early On Matters
items.desc: There's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car accident case, but a recorded statement given too soon to the other driver's insurer can undercut your claim. It's worth talking to someone before you say anything official.

items.question: I was in a crash near Guadalupe Street — do I really need a lawyer for something that seems minor?
items.answer: Not every crash needs one, but injuries don't always show up right away, and insurers sometimes offer a quick settlement before you know the full extent of what's wrong. Talking to an independent attorney costs you nothing through LawProactive, so it's worth a conversation even if the crash seemed small at first.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Guadalupe?
items.answer: In California, you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That timeline can be much shorter — sometimes just six months — if your accident involved a government vehicle or road, like a city-maintained street. An attorney can tell you which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling — should I give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally wise to hold off until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use recorded statements to find inconsistencies or get you to downplay your injuries. LawProactive can connect you with someone who can advise you before you say anything on the record.
